text:
incident-bot: Pager: elevated 5xx and increased tail latency for inference API in az2c (us-west-2c). Metric spike started ~3m ago. Alerts: 5xx-rate > 3% and p99 latency > 1.2s.
maya: taking pager, joining.
maya: looking at graphs, spike correlated with a sharp increase in connection resets from our inference nodes to the local resolver and NLB targets.
kevin: seeing same, `tcpdump` shows repeated SYN then RST from instance side. Possible sticky connections / flow table exhaustion on host.
jonah: traced to resolver latency + SYN retries -> healthchecks failing for some NLB targets, traffic shifting to fewer healthy nodes -> overload -> 502s.
linda: any customer impact?
maya: early numbers: about 0.9% of total requests getting 502/timeouts in the last 5m, higher for ~us-west-2c-only customers. A few enterprise customers on reserved capacity show degraded tail latency.
ralph: pinging CS to draft a note if this persists.
kevin: quick check: instance metrics show increased `netdev->rx_drops` and `tx_queue_len` spikes on a subset of g4dn nodes. Could be NIC offload or driver regression combined with resolver backpressure.
maya: trying to force NLB healthcheck config to use TCP rather than HTTP for now to reduce backend resets.
eng-bot: Deploy bot: started `route-failover-usw2a` traffic policy change (dry-run) by maya.
maya: initiating emergency steering: increase route weight to us-west-2a by 80% for inference-prod pool for 1m windows. Command: `rdctl traffic steer --from=usw2c --to=usw2a --weight=0.8 --reason="az2c conn resets"`
kevin: also increasing node-level socket backlog and enabling syn-queue bump on affected hosts as short-term mitigation: `sysctl -w net.core.somaxconn=1024 net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog=2048` applied to autoscaling group.
jonah: confirm NLB target deregistration is causing sticky session rebinds? If targets go unhealthy, clients reconnect and pile onto remaining nodes -> cascading overload.
linda: can we fallback to a smaller model variant to reduce per-request resource pressure while we stabilize?
maya: yes initiating model fallback for routing policy: switching new requests in us-west-2c to `redwood-small-v1` (compat mode) with quicker token budget for the next 10m. Command: `rdctl model switch --region=usw2c --from=redwood-std-v1 --to=redwood-small-v1 --ttl=600s`
kevin: DNS resolver lookups from instances show 50-100ms spikes and occasional `SERVFAIL`. Suspect resolver host in AZ under strain. We're adding a fallback resolver config to instances: `options timeout:2 attempts:2 rotate` and `resolvconf` update. Rolling patch out via SSM to the affected fleet.
eng-bot: SSM patch job started: `ssm-patch/resolver-backoff-412887` by kevin.
maya: traffic steer complete. Observing immediate drop in 5xx to ~0.4% and p99 latency coming down.
jonah: good. Still seeing a small subset of instances with net drops; keeping an eye on rx_errors.
linda: customer comm: Ralph, please prepare a short update: acknowledging issue, mitigation in progress, potential short degraded tail latency for customers in us-west-2c, ETA ~30m.
ralph: on it, drafting now.
kevin: plan for root cause: need to investigate NIC driver and resolver host capacity; open follow-up ticket to infra-team to repro at scale.
maya: creating incident doc in ops board: https://redwood.ops/incidents/4128879999 (will paste summary).
jonah: recommend we enable NLB connection draining longer to avoid abrupt target rebalancing as part of follow-up.
maya: handing off to kevin for next 30m — I'm rotating off in 25m. kevin, take ownership if anything regresses.
kevin: taking handoff. I'll monitor for 1h and start deeper infra debugging.
eng-bot: Incident timeline note appended by eng-bot: mitigation actions (traffic steer, model fallback, sysctl bump, resolver fallback) recorded.
maya: thanks team. Will update PS hour status and then off. :thumbsup:
